Technological developments and digitization has redefined how markets operate. There are cyber-security risks to consider. There is social media to monitor. Even preferences are changing. We have a new breed of financial consumers who are young, upwardly mobile, and technology-savvy. It is a more impatient and demanding consumer base. To service this base, there is enhanced competition. There is globalization, regional integration. Information in itself is a prized, valued, and fiercely protected commodity. In considering legislative initiatives, we must have these new trends in mind. In the BSP, we are conscious of this and are working to provide an enabling regulatory environment for fin-tech while balancing the need to maintain prudent credit underwriting and technology risk management and to uphold information security standards. The BSP supports a Senate Bill on Cybercrime Prevention which redefines offenses of aiding, abetting and attempting to commit cybercrime; imposing a higher penalty for violations committed using information and communications technology; and the addition of a provision that prosecution under the law shall be without prejudice to liability under the Revised Penal Code or other special laws. The BSP also endorses enactment of a Payment Systems Act for a safer, more efficient and reliable operation of payment systems to control systemic risk. Some key proposals include granting the BSP formal authority over payment systems with authority to coordinate with other government agencies and overseers of payment systems of other countries to facilitate safe, efficient and reliable cross-border payment transactions. To address the global community's call for a more transparent financial system while protecting the rights of bank depositors from unwarranted intrusion, and to enable more effective investigation of questionable actions and the prosecution of money launderers, the BSP endorses amendment of the law on Secrecy of Bank Deposits and the Foreign Currency Deposit Act. Recent events have also highlighted the urgency to amend the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA): to strengthen the BSP's authority to look into deposits when checking AMLA compliance; to allow disclosure to BSP of Covered Transaction and Suspicious Transaction Report information; to designate BSP as supervising authority of foreign exchange dealers, money changers, and remittance and transfer companies for AMLA purposes; to increase the amount of administrative penalties for AMLA violations and to spread a wider and more effective net to include casinos and other non-banks among AMLA covered entities. (Daming information nito... siguro puede pang MCLE compliance.) Legislative Initiative: to Protect Earlier Gains Kidding aside, ladies and gentlemen, despite challenges in the external environment, the Philippine economy continues to expand. Our growth in the first quarter of 2017 was characterized by manageable inflation and more than adequate gross international reserves. Overseas Filipino remittances, revenue from the business process outsourcing sector and tourism income contribute to higher consumption spending. Solid macroeconomic fundamentals are buffers against potential external shocks and the BSP continues to strengthen its framework for financial risk surveillance. We do this with tools within the limits of our present charter, Republic Act No. 7653. These tools are twenty-four (24) years old! To strengthen these tools, supplement mechanisms for the protection of depositor savings, ensure the smooth flow of financial system transactions, as well as enhance its corporate viability, the amendment of the BSP Charter is on the very top of our legislative agenda. Republic Act No. 7653 was passed more than 2 decades ago. As I have mentioned, the economic and financial landscape here and overseas has changed significantly in scale, scope, reach, and complexity. There is thus urgency in having the proposed amendments passed to enable BSP to formulate and implement even better and more timely policies and programs to achieve price stability. Amendments will allow BSP to act even more swiftly to ensure that supervised institutions are doing business in a safe and sound manner with a healthy discipline for risk-taking activities. Salient in our proposed charter amendments are: the formal recognition of financial stability as a BSP mandate; oversight of the payment and settlement systems; authority to require data and information from non-banks and enhanced supervisory and regulatory powers, among others. We believe that a stronger BSP will translate to a more stable and resilient macroeconomy and a robust Philippine financial system that is attractive to investments and businesses to generate employment and promote inclusive growth. We believe this is how the legislative framework can improve to protect earlier and future gains. Legislative Reforms to Promote Sustained and Inclusive Growth At the heart of my governorship is the desire to bring BSP closer to the public it serves. In the BSP, we firmly believe that for economic growth and progress to be more meaningful, its benefits, the products that allow people to save, borrow, invest and insure risks must be made available to them. In the BSP, we have reformed the regulatory framework for allowing this to happen... to increase financial access and usage points for our countrymen, beyond brick and mortar bank buildings. We collaborate and cooperate with stakeholders from the private and public sectors to build a more inclusive financial system, focusing on increasing financial literacy and education and consumer protection. What was once only a flagship advocacy has now become a compelling purpose with departments within the BSP created for this very end: the Inclusive Finance Advocacy Office, the Financial Consumer Protection Department and the Economic and Financial Learning Center. We have worked with Congress to push bills to promote inclusive financial growth. We were heartened with the passing of Republic Act No. 10744, granting juridical personality to existing and future Credit Surety Fund Cooperatives, so that the credit-worthiness of micro, small and medium enterprises would be increased and so that they would be able to obtain loans from banks. We recently launched the Personal Equity and Retirement Account System under Republic Act No. 9505. The PERA promotes capital market development and long-term savings mobilization, allowing persons with a capacity to contract (and with Tax Identification Numbers) to voluntarily open personal accounts with banks and invest in certain products to save more for their retirement. But there is still much to be done with respect to financial inclusion. The BSP is pushing for the Bill on the Enactment of Islamic Banking in the Philippines. We aim to develop a suitable and clear legal and regulatory framework to promote a truly responsive Islamic banking system that positively complements the existing conventional banking system. The Decision: Becoming Advocates What now? How can we be partners in working for a more enabling and responsive legal environment that will foster a safer, more efficient, reliable and inclusive financial system? I began with a narrative of my first-year law experience. Some of you may wonder why I did not continue with law school... Even then I was already a young economist of the Central Bank. I recognized a trade-off. I was a working student and law school was taking a toll on the pursuit of my chosen career. I had to choose where I wanted to excel. And I made my strategic decision... Recognizing trade-offs, deciding and acting on costs and benefits, we do this every day, perhaps every hour. I would like to close with the message that yes, there is a trade-off in working towards a more responsive legal framework. But we must focus on the gains... gains for not just one sector or group... but gains for the nation as a whole. There is a cost to financial exclusion and a very clear and meaningful benefit to financial inclusion. I urge you... as fellow professionals who engage in meaningful internal discourses... as fellow Filipinos who know the value of the one hand and the other... to partner with us as advocates of financial inclusion, as advocates for a more responsive legal framework for economic and financial stability. A way this is done is through discourse (Socratic or otherwise) and collaboration with peers and colleagues, with regulatory and supervisory authorities, with stakeholders, with government... even with your students. You are all in a position to influence the narrative of how our laws evolve - as predicted by Justice Holmes, and as desired by posterity. The BSP relies on your support. We hope you will come to this decision. Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat. Mabuhay ang Philippine Bar Association. Mabuhay ang mahal nating Pilipinas.

Title: Bangko Sentral Mandates and How They Help Maintain a Stable Business Environment
Occasion: Wallace Business Forum Roundtable
Speaker: Nestor A. Espenilla, Jr.
Text: Chairman and President, Mr. Peter Wallace, Excellencies, distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen, thank you for having me in your company this morning. I assumed office as Governor of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas twenty-three (23) days ago, on July 3... Thus, some, or most of you, might be wondering what kind of changes will be instituted, and how new policies under my governorship (if any), might affect the Philippine business environment... These are valid musings. Ladies and gentlemen, I reiterate my intention that the next six years of my being at BSP's helm will be characterized by continuity - more specifically, "continuity plus plus" - a line, that to my surprise, gained some popularity upon my appointment. I may interest you to know that the phrase, "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" as initially documented, is attributed to Burt Lance, Director of the Office of Management and Budget under U.S. President Jimmy Carter?... I find it interesting that this was first used in a public service context. My predecessor (former BSP Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.) left a strong and resilient Philippine economy, a stable banking system, and a safe and reliable payments system (among other accomplishments) as legacies... Continuity is not just desirable, it is necessary. Macroeconomic Policies Our economy continues to expand. The Philippines is in a position of strength notwithstanding external challenges. We have had manageable inflation and high growth. The 2017 inflation outturn still well-within the National Government target range of 2-4 pct... Our updated forecast over the policy horizon is that inflation would still be within the target range of 2-4 pct and probably staying close to the mid-point. The numbers look good. This notwithstanding, BSP will continue to monitor shifts in market sentiment along with trends in commodity prices and other inflation drivers. As always, BSP will be continually refreshing its liquidity forecasting and inflation models so they are in tune with evolving impulses. But no significant deviation from previous monetary policy approach is anticipated. We can continue to rely on the BSP's flexible inflation targeting mechanism periodic review of monetary policy, and transparent communication of policy decisions. I realize that this - inflation targeting - may sound esoteric. But, really, the goals are down-to-earth.... This particular BSP focus has very practical significance - to those in this ballroom! Maintaining price stability by keeping inflation low and stable reduces uncertainty and allows businessmen and investors (like yourselves) to better plan and make informed consumption, investment, saving, and production decisions... Thus, at its very heart, the BSP's primary mandate is central to fostering a stable business environment... We are fully dedicated to this responsibility and we hope you would regard us as strong partners in this respect. Strong and Stable Banking System Team BSP under Governor Tetangco also did very well in working for the fulfillment of the BSP's second mandate. Through the BSP's pursuit of progressive and prudent banking reforms, our banking system currently enjoys double-digit growth in resources, expansion in lending, adequate capitalization at levels above both the national requirement of 10 pct and the Basel Committee norm of 8 pct. Philippine banks continue to have improved asset quality and profitable operations. Significantly bringing this about was the alignment of our regulatory frameworks with international standards (such as Basel Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision) while remaining sensitive to domestic conditions. Notably, BSP adopted a corporate governance framework emphasizing the responsibilities and qualifications of the bank's board of directors and senior management. The BSP is currently phasing-in the issuance of enhanced guidelines which will further integrate risk management and responsible conduct to the overall governance framework. We also enhanced local standards on risk-based capital and risk-management practices of banks to allow them to withstand internal and external shocks. A strong and stable banking system translates to development for the rest of the nation, as banks support the financing needs of our continuously growing economy and allocate resources efficiently. Again, a practical goal. BSP and Bankers of the Wallace Business Forum While bankers would deem the BSP, as first and foremost, their supervisor/regulator - I ask (of the bankers inside and outside of this room) that another dimension be added to this perspective: that the BSP be viewed as a partner (Yes, even of its supervised entities!). This proposition is not too alien... with respect the regulations and reforms I mentioned, there has always been close consultation with the banks. When this reforms were instituted there was a phasing-in with BSP allowing parallel run periods for banks to gain familiarity BSP's new conduct of supervision. Banks were also given time to build up capital as required under the new Basel standards. The result of this partnership is that banks are better-run and adequately capitalized. I believe that when rules and regulations are merely imposed from the top-down, results can be unsustainable. For sustainability, the interests of the supervisor/regulator and the regulated must converge. This convergence in essence, births a strong partnership. We would agree that common ground is found in our shared desire to maintain an environment that encourages and is conducive to progressive business and healthy competition. BSP Initiatives: Stronger Business Environment For the last twenty-four (24) years since its establishment in 1993, the BSP has worked towards this end. Let me cite six (6) recent and concrete examples of our initiatives to accomplish this purpose (These examples are in no particular order): First, the BSP was instrumental to the approval of Republic Act No. 10641 further liberalizing the entry of foreign banks into the Philippines. With this law, foreign banks may establish or acquire up to 100 percent of the voting stock of an existing domestic bank or to put up a branch. To accept this as a gain may seem counter-intuitive to local bankers as it has the effect of fostering strong competition. The benefit desired is for the long-run as it paves the way for foreign banks to serve as vehicles for foreign direct investments into the Philippines. Also the increase in competition pressures allows a leveling-up of services and less complacency. Sophisticated players that can offer financial technology solutions have already entered the market, ushering in a notable, gradual unbundling of the traditional value chain. The competition will make everyone work harder and seek new markets that hitherto not been well-served. The same benefits can be said to stem from the BSP's implementation of the ASEAN Banking Integration Framework (ABIF). Second, since 2007, the BSP has been introducing waves of FX regulatory reforms to address the dynamic needs of the Philippine economy that have evolved with the interconnection of global markets. Regulations were amended to raise the FX threshold residents can purchase from the banking system. This allows the sale of FX for settlement of resident-to-resident transactions, relieving the private sector from securing prior BSP approval and registration requirements. Moreover, to ensure greater transparency in the FX market, BSP continues to develop regulations to cover non-bank entities including money service businesses. These efforts to liberalize the FX market are forward-looking and geared towards regional integration. Our next moves will be increasingly more ambitious. We are liberalizing further registration and approval rules for foreign borrowings and investments to eliminate red tape and capture more information. Third, the BSP established the Interest Rate Corridor System (IRC). The objective is to make market interest rates move closer to the BSP policy rate. In the long run, this supports Philippine capital markets by encouraging money market transactions and better liquidity management. These lie as the key foundation of a well-function domestic debt market. You may agree with me that active money market transactions promote real price discovery and transparency. Thus, the IRC will lead to the generation of more reasonable interest rate benchmarks that enable effective and efficient pricing of financial products in the local market. Fourth, to ensure an efficient payment and settlement system, the BSP adopted the National Retail Payments System (NRPS), a flagship program for digital finance. The NRPS bridges the country's transition from a cash-heavy economy, where 99 percent of transactions are done in cash, to a cash-lite economy, where at least 20 percent of retail transactions by volume will go electronic. BSP is mindful that innovations, particularly financial technology, reduces costs and accelerates the on-boarding of currently excluded markets into the formal financial system. I think this trend of modernization that supports e-commerce is also of particular interest to business people such as yourselves. But let me also quickly point out, that even as we embrace technology, we are also very cognizant of new risks and have introduced enhanced rules to control cyber-crime and other technology risks. Fifth, BSP took a primary role in amending the Anti-money Laundering Act. AMLA rules have expanded to cover non-bank financial institutions such as pawnshops and money service businesses. Recently, President Duterte signed a law amending the AMLA to cover casinos. (While the list can still go on), I will cite as my final and Sixth example, the BSP's initiatives in helping develop a deeper, more efficient and integrated domestic financial and capital market. The BSP, Bureau of the Treasury, Securities and Exchange Commission and the Department of Finance are jointly proposing an operational roadmap for local currency debt market development. Three areas are prioritized: (1) the creation of reliable financial benchmarks and valuation of financial instruments; (2) deepening the local bond market by adopting reforms in the primary dealer system, increasing supply of short-term debt securities, and developing an effective regulatory framework for the derivatives and repo markets; and (3) the establishment of an integrated financial market infrastructure to promote price discovery, transparency and orderly trading, clearing, and settlement of the full range of financial transactions. More inclusive financial system As I close, allow me to speak about the need to work towards greater financial inclusion. I saved this for last not because of its insignificance. Quite the opposite. It is most important and is the "plus plus" in "continuity plus plus." I speak of Financial Inclusion often and with passion. With conviction, I have said that for progress to be meaningful, it must be inclusive; that Filipinos from the grassroots, at the peripheries, must be given usage and access to financial services that will allow them to save, invest and borrow for productive uses. Our countrymen must be provided with financial literacy and education so that they may make informed financial decisions to better their lives and that of their families. It sounds like a matter of corporate social responsibility... It sounds like a charitable endeavor. But, friends, esteemed pillars of the business community, may I stress that the drive for financial inclusion is not just this. As business people, it is understandable that the primordial concern is the bottom line. But let me put forward - or reintroduce - a revolutionary thought. (This is not original). Perhaps you are familiar with C.K. Prahalad's theory on "the bottom of the pyramid"? The idea is that those in the lowest socio-economic group is actually a large and profitable consumer base! This is a demographic to be empowered: First, as a financially literate populace; Next, as active and thoughtful consumers! This is an exciting prospect that we hope you, our partners in business and industry would support the BSP in achieving. On the BSP's part, we spearhead the implementation of the National Strategy for Financial Inclusion to make the financial system accessible and responsive to the needs of the entire population, to support a broad based and inclusive growth. There is still much to be done. We count on you, our partners in the Wallace Business Forum to help usher in the ideal of financial inclusion and to work with us more closely, collaborating towards maintaining a more stable, conducive and stronger business environment. Thank you for your kind attention.

Title: Building on Built Foundations: Continuity and Change
Location: Manila Golf and Country Club, Makati City
Occasion: Fellows Meeting of the Foundation of Economic Freedom
Speaker: Nestor A. Espenilla, Jr.
Text: Former Central Bank Governor and Ambassador Jose Cuisia... Monetary Board Member and Foundation for Economic Freedom (FEF) Trustee Philip Medalla... SEC Commissioner Ephyro Amatong... FEF Chair Bobby Ocampo... FEF Vice-Chair Romy Bernardo... FEF President Toti Chikiamco... members of the Board of Trustees of the FEF... Executive Director Peter Perfecto of the Makati Business Club... friends from the US Embassy led by Mr. David Schnier... esteemed guests, ladies and gentlemen, good evening! I thank the FEF for the invitation to speak at this Fellows meeting. And what a group of distinguished Fellows it is! Giants of Philippine business, banking and financial industries, the academe and government... The energy in this room is palpable and I am happy to be among like-minded Filipinos with a heart for economic liberty and good governance. Tonight, I am among former bosses, colleagues, and friends who know me better as "DG Nesting" - Deputy Governor of the BSP's Supervision and Examination Sector (an integral part of my identity since 2005). Twenty-three (23) days ago, on July 3, 2017, things changed (quite dramatically for me), and I now have the privilege to represent the remarkable institution that is the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, as its Governor and as Chairperson of the Monetary Board...I am both deeply humbled and proud to do so. In FEF President Chikiamco's letter invitation - which I received sometime in May, soon after I was announced, - the request was specifically for me to speak about my "plans for continuity and change in the BSP as incoming BSP Governor." That there is room - No, that there is necessity - for both continuity and change is a simple but very powerful idea. Often, we think of the two concepts as mutually exclusive/ as an either/or... as two ideals on polar ends of a dichotomy... But this is not necessarily true. For even as I stand here and look around this room, I see where both continuity (stability) and change (dynamism) combine and reconcile for the good of our nation. All of us here, have in one way or another, been entrusted with building on the foundations built by those who came before us. We do not start from scratch. There is no tabula rasa in the task of achieving national development. The challenge is to find balance between steadfastness and progress given the demands and specificities of the times... Somehow (despite the initial excitement), when I first learned of my appointment as BSP Governor, I was able to articulate this need for equilibrium in the phrase, "continuity plus plus." It is a phrase that has gained some popularity (especially with media) in predicting how my term will be. In the phrase, there is recognition that change is a given, but a stable and familiar anchor is essential to move new initiatives forward effectively. Stability Amidst Change Greek Philosoper, Heraclitus said, "change is the only constant in life." This may very well describe our economic journey. We are fortunate that despite challenging times brought about by the US Fed rate hike, Brexit, geopolitical events in the Middle East and North Asia, and lingering global market uncertainties, the domestic economy continues to be in a relative position of strength. The Philippines is still one of the region's fastest growing economies, with growth solidly anchored on sound macroeconomic policies. Domestic inflation remains to be manageable because it is low and stable. It is within Government's target and is aligned with market expectation. Domestic liquidity is adequate to support further economic expansion. Money supply grew by 11.3 percent to P9.6 trillion as of end-May 2017. Accordingly, total credits to the private sector grew by 18.3 percent, driven by a sustained increase in bank lending which expanded by 17.8 percent year-on-year. And credit growth is not necessarily associated with weakening asset quality, precisely because of lessons learned. The country's external position is strong. Gross international reserves (GIR) at US$81.3 billion can cover 8.6 months' worth of imports as of end-June 2017. This is equivalent to 5.4 times the country's short-term external debt based on original maturity, and 4.0 times based on residual maturity. For the first quarter of 2017, the country's outstanding external debt declined by 1.3 percent quarter-on-quarter (QoQ) to US$73.8 billion. The maturity profile of these debts is mostly in the medium to long-term. Sufficient buffers and longer maturity of debts ease foreign exchange requirements for debt servicing. The banking system likewise continues to be a source of strength and is well-positioned to further support domestic economic needs. Banks have stronger balance sheets with steady growth in assets, loans, deposits and capital. Asset quality significantly improved as the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio stood at 2.0 percent as of end-May 2017. Compare this with its peak of 16.9 percent in 2001! Banks are liquid with an assets-to-deposits ratio of 49.6 percent during the same period. Banks are likewise well-capitalized with the capital adequacy ratio (CAR) at 15.3 percent as of end-March 2017. Overall, banks are sound and profitable. These numbers demonstrate how banks successfully adjusted to the challenging external environment and the evolving landscape. Continuity and "the Plus-Plus" I am blessed that Team BSP under Governor Say Tetangco left a legacy of excellence. What a solid and formidable foundation to continue building on! In Homer's Odyssey, when the king of Ithaca fought in the Trojan War, he entrusted his son and household to a reliable aide named, Mentor. In time, the word "mentor" has become synonymous with the "advisor, friend, teacher and counselor." History is replete with examples of meaningful mentor-mentee relationships. There is Socrates and Plato, Haydn and Beethoven, Emerson and Thoreau and even Buffet and Gates!... How fortunate I am that in my thirty-six (36) years of being a Central Banker, I can add the mentorship provided me by Governor Tetangco and the illustrious Governors before him starting from Governor Laya. It is because of the example and mentorship that I can dare, with Team BSP, to insightfully identify components of the "plus plus" and work purposely and decisively on them. Under my watch, the BSP will continue to focus on financial sector policy reforms. The interest rate corridor (IRC) system was implemented last year. With this, we have started to move forward, to make the conduct of monetary policy more efficient and market-oriented. Our agenda is to further refine the IRC and to progressively dial down onerous reserve requirements whenever the timing is right. BSP is also highly supportive of capital market reforms. The aim is to provide a viable alternative source of financing for long-term investments, including the development of the necessary financial market infrastructures (FMI). Last year, we started the groundwork for enabling prudent project financing under Circular No. 914. It revisits the concept of SBL to create space for self-sustaining big ticket projects. The BSP is likewise actively collaborating with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) and the DOF to further accelerate the development of the domestic debt market. Market participants will soon be engaged to discuss an operational roadmap. In the works is a sequenced approach to implement key reforms to develop the local currency debt market. We believe this is a crucial component to sustain the economy's growth momentum. Further liberalization of existing rules on foreign exchange transactions is necessary to achieve a more risk-focused, transparent and market-determined policy framework. Notwithstanding waves of liberalization, we recognize that the foreign exchange market framework remains restrictive, difficult, opaque, and shallow. It is a throwback to a time when foreign exchange was scarce, our reserves so meagre, and market confidence was low. Today, it is an impediment to growth and adds to the cost of doing business. We will continue to reshape the financial system so that it is fully responsive to the needs of the domestic economy. The enabling regulatory environment for fin-tech and digital finance needs to be developed without sacrificing prudent credit underwriting, market integrity, consumer protection, and information security standards. The digitalization of finance is essential to achieve significant inroad against financial exclusion and payments inefficiency. Parallel to this is the commitment to advance our financial inclusion agenda, with the goal of furthering financial education and consumer protection. The day will soon come where financial consumers and investors will have an increased ability to make informed business decisions with options from a longer, fresher and more innovative menu of available financial products and services. Legal Framework Initiatives At noon today, I spoke to the Philippine Bar Association. I shared with them the necessity to evaluate our current legal framework for economics, banking and finance. It is important to consider if the current legal framework is attuned to the changing economic and financial environment... if it is poised to protect our earlier gains... and if it is sufficient to promote sustainable economic growth. A lively discussion followed after the challenge was posed. I had the opportunity to share with them BSP's initiatives in working closely with both Houses of Congress for the enactment of laws to create an even stronger and more enabling legal environment compatible with aspiration of high growth and more equitable economy. I shared with them the move to amend the BSP Charter (which is twenty-four (24) years old), the Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA) (which was recently amended when President Duterte signed a law to include casinos in the list of covered persons), and the Deposit Secrecy Law to allow transparency and enable swifter and more efficient investigation of questionable actions and the prosecution of money launderers while protecting the rights of bank depositors from unwarranted intrusion. I also spoke about the enactment of a Payments System Act to formalize BSP's oversight of the national payment system. This will build trust and confidence that are necessary to grow our payments system. I disclosed that the promulgation of an Islamic Banking Law to revitalize Islamic banking in the Philippines by allowing greater participation in the market is also a priority. I shared that BSP also intends to provide a harmonized legal framework for pooled vehicles of investments through a Collective Investment Schemes Law. I spoke as well of our strong support for the establishment of a National ID System that will promote financial integrity, inclusion, and transparency. Closing Remarks Ladies and gentlemen, there is much to be done and it is through our collaboration and partnership that we will be able to sustain our growth momentum. All of us here are involved in an ever continuing endeavour. In our various fields, torches are passed from one leader to another, with mentors imparting wisdom and guidance, not to foster stagnation but to champion improvement and development... In the BSP, while there was a changing of the guard, the mandates remain the same. We shall persist in the pursuit of these mandates, with greater vigour and more imagination. In doing so, we are, as always, grateful for your invaluable partnership and support. Maraming salamat po sa Foundation for Economic Freedom for bravely espousing progressive economic policies that make for a better, more prosperous, and fairer society. Mabuhay po tayong lahat!

Title: BSP and BAIPHIL Moving Mountains: New Heights in Banking Excellence
Location: Rizal Ballroom C of the Makati Shangri-La Hotel
Occasion: the Induction Ceremony and General Membership Meeting of the Bankers Institute of the Philippines (BAIPHIL)
Speaker: Nestor A. Espenilla, Jr.
Text: Distinguished Monetary Board Colleagues, Juan de Zuniga and Tony Abacan, BAIPHIL President Irene Arroyo, immediate past President, Liza Ortiz, other BAIPHIL past presidents, BAIPHIL directors, officers and members, BAP President Nestor V. Tan, bank CEOs, my PDIC colleagues, esteemed guests, friends, fellow BSPers past and present, ladies and gentlemen, good afternoon! It is an honor and pleasure to carry on the tradition of inducting the new board members and officers of BAIPHIL. As new BSP Governor... [I assumed the post eleven (11) days ago]... it is auspicious that I now address the new leadership of BAIPHIL...On behalf of my colleagues in BSP and the Monetary Board, let me extend our congratulations. As new leaders, it is natural for us to aspire greater achievements for the teams we lead. This is why I find your theme: "Scaling New Heights in Banking Excellence" very engaging. The theme is both timely and relevant as we come into our fresh roles and as the financial system evolves. The theme mentions heights. To add imagery to this message, let me take Mt. Everest as a starting point. Everest, known as the roof of the world stands twenty-nine thousand and thirty-five (29,035) feet above sea level. This is the ultimate goal of hard-core mountain climbers, the highest of heights. On 29 May 1953, a New Zealander, Sir Edmund Hillary and a Sherpa, Tenzing Norgay, successfully climbed Mt. Everest in the face of great risk. As documented, they were the very first mountain climbers to reach the summit. Now, sixty-four (64) years later, the peak of Everest is decidedly less lonely and more than 3,500 climbers have already reached the top or "summitted". A myriad of things have changed since then. But from the time it was first done to the present day, scaling Everest or any mountain, consistently demands: First: intense training and preparation; Second: sensitivity to the environment and possible changes to climate; Third: possession of well-maintained equipment; Fourth: a team of highly trusted and reliable individuals; Fifth: leadership of competent guides; and Finally: tenacity and courage to keep going amidst challenges. Training and Preparation In mountain climbing, each team member has to be skilled, fit, and prepared physically and mentally. This takes years of conditioning if one is to take on the tasks involved. As the banking industry's premier training arm, BAIPHIL plays an important role in providing required skill sets and competencies for modern banking. BSP commends BAIPHIL for continually being proactive in responding to the training gaps and emerging requirements of the banking industry in line with on-going developments in the regulatory and operating environment. With its expertise, synergy and collaborative partnership with the BSP, BAIPHIL is in the best position to design a comprehensive training program to foster and strengthen expertise, excellence and integrity among banking professionals. Environmental Sensitivity The conditions for climbing higher look good! The Philippine economy remains in a position of strength. It continues to expand, despite challenges in the external environment. This expansion is increasingly broad-based with notable rebound in agriculture and exports sectors. The sustained strength of the economy in the first quarter of 2017 was underpinned by manageable inflation, more than adequate gross international reserves and a steady stream of inflows from overseas Filipino remittances, revenue from the business process outsourcing sector and tourism income, all contributing to higher consumption spending. Moreover, the Philippine banking system continues to be a stable anchor for the economy with key performance indicators showing double-digit growth in resources, expansion in lending, adequate capitalization, improved asset quality, and profitable operations. These gains driven by our common vision will fuel us to pursue greater heights. Well-Maintained Equipment and Gear As Central Monetary Authority, the BSP has a well-articulated policy framework and an enhanced policy tool kit. Like good and ready mountain climbers, our gear is ready and we have improved surveillance methods. Assessing the mountain, we are thoughtful about weather shifts. For instance, the increasingly clear signal for policy normalization in advanced western economies points to a rise in global interest rates, just a question of timing and pace. Mindful of these, BSP continually strengthens its framework for financial risk surveillance, sharpening assessment of market conditions. We consider the interconnectedness of economic agents, credit concentration and liquidity, and the evaluation and pricing of risks. Our approach is pre-emptive to mitigate any undue risk build-up in the financial system, but we have also built up solid macroeconomic fundamentals that serve as buffers to weather potential external shocks. These safeguards notwithstanding, BSP continues to refine existing early warning systems, distress indices and stress tests. BSP is constantly developing financial and economic models that improve our understanding of how relevant variables move. Trusted and Dedicated Team To be successful in mountain climbing (like facing the challenges of the banking industry) one cannot go up alone. It is not a solitary undertaking. Climbers must learn the basics from other climbers, as well as help each other up from time to time. In our industry, this means we must develop close collaborations and relationships and encourage communication. I am fortunate that I have inherited a very capable and competent team BSP where each public servant contributes to the fulfilment of our mandates. We can also depend on the collaboration and synergies among valued stakeholders like BAIPHIL. Indeed we cannot do it alone. Competent Leadership Ladies and gentlemen, possessing close familiarity with "the mountain and mountains" of banking, we could consider the Bangko Sentral and BAIPHIL as the industry's 'sherpas'. We provide guidance and direction to others in the industry as we walk the same path. We guide towards the shared vision of upholding a stable and inclusive banking system. Under my stewardship, this will be pursued with fervour. As our fellow Sherpa, the BSP counts on BAIPHIL to take on even greater significance in this age of global convergence. Together, we have to prepare the banking community by anticipating harder but more fulfilling climbs ahead. Through continuous training and education, the banking profession will be better equipped and prepared to keep pace with the ever evolving financial services industry. Tenacity and Courage In the book, "The Last Step: The American Ascent of K2" / it is said that, "the courage of mountain climbers is not blind, inexplicable, meaningless; it is courage with ability, brains, and tenacity of purpose." In this industry, this is the same brand of courage we must have to achieve our goal of banking and financial stability. Our courage is not based on a false sense of security. But we are motivated to always raise the bar of professional excellence and business integrity for banks. We have the determination and passion to excel in our current craft, of pursuing excellence and constantly improving our work so that we could deliver the best financial services to the Filipino consumer and our country. Moving Mountains That I used Mt. Everest in an analogy to illustrate our present and on-going journey together is perhaps ambitious enough... And while I have built parallelisms between the two endeavours, I dare say that in our industry the mountains are not static. Banking is not unmoving like the formidable Everest. There is no final peak to overcome. The Bangko Sentral celebrated its twenty-fourth (24) anniversary last week. I have been a Central Banker for the last thirty-six (36) years. BAIPHIL marked its seventy-sixth (76th) year this June. As veterans in this field, we know that in banking and in central banking, the process of scaling new heights is an active and continuing endeavour. Friends: banking products, financial services and needs, technology and consumer preferences are always levelling up. We have to keep pace. We do this with training and education. We do this with updated and relevant regulations. We do this with partnership as we are confronted with an evolving market landscape of international standards and prudential regulations. Our shared strategy necessitates taking a more holistic view of these developments. We do this too by strengthening corporate governance standards and risk management practices. We at the BSP have raised the bar of prudential standards to promote resilience in the banking system and market discipline for risk-taking activities. Because of growing regional financial integration and the entry of foreign banks, competition pressures have increased. New sophisticated players such as financial technology solution providers have entered the market. This is a good thing as these bring about a notable and gradual unbundling of the traditional value chain in the Philippines and intimately links banks closer to customers. While FinTech provides interconnectivity, convenience, and efficiency in delivery of financial products and services, we must also be vigilant as it also ushers in cyber-security concerns. In this regard, the BSP has been laying the groundwork on promoting cyber-security and related regulation on technology. But there is still much to be done. Ladies and gentlemen, we know from science that the mountains are moving due to continental drift and that we, BSP and BAIPHIL, must therefore continue to move with the mountains even as we scale the one in front of us. In Closing: Inclusion as We Climb I'd like to think also that there are several summits in banking and central banking... That as one reaches a vantage point, more and more of the surrounds are taken into perspective... As one climbs, one's view becomes wider. I have heard from mountain climbers that when you reach the top, it is actually quite a humbling experience. I certainly felt that way when I climbed Mt. Fuji as a millennial graduate student in Japan in 1988. At higher heights, one sees the bigger picture more clearly and wishes for others to experience the same. The same holds true as we experience more economic gains and successes. We want more and more people - our countrymen - to be included in the experience. Our goal is for more of our countrymen to save and borrow for productive uses, avail of investment and insurance products, and send and receive payments securely and efficiently. We firmly believe that this financial empowerment is the only way for economic growth to be truly meaningful. We trust in BAIPHIL to help us move this vision forward. BAIPHIL can in turn count on the full support of the BSP for its future endeavours. Mabuhay ang BAIPHIL at BSP! Maraming salamat po!

Title: Turning Vision Into Partnership
Occasion: Awards Ceremony and Appreciation Lunch
Speaker: Nestor A. Espenilla, Jr.
Text: PDIC President Roberto Tan, National Statistician Lisa Bersales, Members of the Monetary Board, sector heads, fellow BSPers, former Central Bank Governor Jaime C. Laya, guests, a pleasant good morning to all of you. Magandang umaga especially to our stakeholders and awardees. Every year for the last fourteen (14) years we at the BSP have held this annual ceremony traditionally right around this time: our Anniversary month... There is significance in this chosen timing. The message we wish to convey is that, not only do we value you: our stakeholders... More so, we recognize that the BSP would not have achieved all it has if it were not for your partnership. This is why we celebrate with you during our milestone month of July. The theme of our 24th Anniversary here at the BSP is "together moving forward: a new season of excellence." There is a journey implied, and a needed collaboration and cooperation expressed. This theme includes, not just the members of the BSP family progressing onward in unity, but this includes you too, our esteemed stakeholders, whom we honor today. I have been with the BSP - then, the Central Bank of the Philippines - since 1981... And as a young Central Banker one of my tasks was to draft technical speeches... So even thirty-six (36) years after, I still have a passion for words. Let me focus on this event's keyword. Stakeholder. It sounds quite ominous. Its origin is consistent with this sense of foreboding. The word "stakeholder" first appeared in the Oxford English Dictionary in 1708. It referred to one holding a wager, a bet. Thankfully, for us now, the word has evolved into a dynamic -- even an exciting and active concept, where speculation has no role. As presently understood, stakeholders are partners and can be involved in the successes of an enterprise, from whose accomplishments they too can greatly benefit. The importance of collaboration and partnerships was stressed by Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr. in his two (2) terms at the BSP's helm... Gov. Say repeatedly said that in the BSP, our work could not be accomplished by the BSP working alone, but only through continued discussion and cooperation with others, like government agencies, institutions, other regulatory bodies, private organizations and entities. This is a belief we strongly hold and will continue to hold here in the BSP. This morning we have one-hundred and forty six (146) outstanding partners that we acknowledge. You are government agencies and departments... private businesses... leaders in your respective industries. You, our honorees and stakeholders are here today because you helped the BSP in its programs. But did you know that beyond the altruism you displayed, where you extended assistance willingly and often without expectation of anything in return from the BSP, there was in your actions, a reward that will ultimately redound to the fulfillment of a shared vision and dream? In the BSP, all employees know our vision by heart. Memorize nila ito. Our vision is to be a world-class monetary authority and a catalyst for a globally competitive economy and financial system that delivers a high quality of life for all Filipinos. A high quality of life for all Filipinos. This includes each person here in this Assembly Hall. And with your contribution, with the assistance you gave us, this is precisely what you are helping us achieve. So, for this, we thank you. Please give yourselves a warm round of applause. This is not rhetoric. For example, the outstanding survey respondents and information partners here who assisted the BSP, helped us in formulating data-driven monetary policy. The responses you gave and the information you provided underpinned enabling decisions that allowed the Philippine economy grow by 6.4 percent in the first quarter of 2017. You helped so that the Philippines continues to be one of the fastest growing economies in Asia. Stakeholder participation is essential so that even amidst confounding global developments such as the Brexit and the United States' seeming turn to protectionist policy, we can stand resilient and stay calm, with inflation at 3.1 percent in the first half of 2017, well within the government's inflation target range for the year. Our external payments position remains manageable. Robust remittances from overseas Filipinos and ample receipts from the business process outsourcing sector continue to fuel economic growth. The country's external debt remains at sustainable levels, with the ratio to GDP improving in Q1 2017 to 24.1 percent from 26.5 percent in the same quarter last year. In addition, the country's Gross International Reserves remain more than adequate at US$81.4 billion as of end-June 2017, equivalent to nearly 9.0 months' worth of imports of goods and payment for services and income. These are achievements that were brought about by sound policy-making built on our collective dedication and willingness to cooperate for the sake of something larger than ourselves. In this assembly hall are exemplary partners who have enabled us to carry out programs that reinforce the BSP's three pillars of central banking. You have contributed to BSP's initiatives and programs in financial inclusion and education... consumer protection... payments and settlements... overseas Filipino remittances... coin recirculation... the clean note policy... and demonetization of our new design series currency. The banking system today is very robust and is poised for broader reach and better service. The number of operating banks as of March 2017 is 599 (head offices) with an overall branch network of 10,679 units. Assets of the banking sector also grew by nearly 12.42% percent year-on-year as of December 2016 boosted by an increase in deposits, profits, and fresh equity. No less important, assets grew without compromising their quality. The Philippine banking system's capital adequacy ratio as of Q3 2016 has reached 15.59 percent, almost double the global-minimum. Prudent policy-making has led to a sturdy financial system and a stable economy. The critical contribution of our partners as exemplified through your compliance with the BSP's various surveys, provision of information, and participation in our diverse programs, advocacies and initiatives, assisted the BSP in fulfilling its mandates. To reinforce the importance of data gathering and increasing our interface with the public, we are pleased to announce the formal launching of the user-friendly BSP e-Survey Portal. This online facility will make it easy and convenient for respondents to participate in the surveys of the BSP. The Coordinated Direct Investment Survey went online last June. The Coordinated Portfolio Investment Survey (CPIS) and monthly Cross Border Transactions Survey questionnaires shall be included in the e-Survey by the end of this month. The launch of the BSP e-Survey Portal aims to improve efficiency in generating the Cross Border Transactions Survey results which are used as inputs for the Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Statistics. These indicators help the BSP craft and assess our policy settings. So as you can see, there are more exciting times ahead, more collaboration planned, and better avenues to make them more successful and productive. We look forward to continuing the journey with you. Congratulations to all our stakeholders. Mabuhay kayo. Mabuhay ang BSP. Mabuhay ang ating bansang Pilipinas!

Title: The Philippines and Japan: Enhancing Strategic Partnership
Location: Mayuree 2 Ballroom, Dusit Hotel, Makati City
Occasion: Cocktail Reception hosted by the Philippines-Japan Society, Inc. (PJS) and the Philippines-Japan Economic Cooperation Committee, Inc. (PHILJEC)
Speaker: Nestor A. Espenilla, Jr.
Text: Ambassador Kazuhide Ishikawa, Prime Minister Cesar Virata, distinguished members of the Philippines-Japan Society, Inc. (PJS) led by President, Mr. Francis C. Laurel, and the Philippines-Japan Economic Cooperation Committee, Inc. (PHILJEC) led by Chairman, Mr. Aniceto G. Saludo, Jr., Secretary General JJ Soriano, my BSP colleague Deputy Governor Cyd Amador, esteemed guests, ladies and gentlemen: Good evening (Konbanwa)! What a pleasure and honor it is for me to be here tonight... As recently appointed Governor of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, opportunities to speak before groups and organizations that enhance economic cooperation and greater financial stability in the region, is always a welcome engagement... This goes without saying... But my delight in being able to address this group tonight also has a personal angle, close to my heart. Thirty-one (31) years ago, in 1986, I was a Monbusho scholar... a scholarship I received from the Japanese Government. Through this generous grant, I earned my masters in Policy Science from the Saitama University's National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies (GRIPS) which is now in Tokyo. What a different world it was in 1986! Since then, there have been many rapid developments in technology and we continue to be in a period of an evolving geopolitical and economic climate. Yet, despite all these vast changes, the Philippines-Japan Society has been unwavering in its commitment to foster closer ties between our nations - even as early as 1972, when it was formally established! I likewise commend the Philippines-Japan Economic Cooperation Committee for its steadfast initiatives to promote closer economic ties between the Philippines and Japan. Living and being educated in Japan truly made a positive impact on me. Such that when I addressed the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas for the first time as Governor last week on July 3, my message began by acknowledging the importance of the principle of "kaizen," stressing the need for "continuous improvement," and recognizing it as an evolutionary process. But aside from kaizen, there is much to be learned from Japanese culture... An important observation I made while living in Japan is that while the west cultivates a sense of self that is independent and unique... in Japan, there is an emphasis on cultivating a sense of self vis-à-vis others and society. I believe this emphasis on harmony and collaboration accounts for our countries' long-standing relationship. Cooperation between our nations has paved the way for the advancement of our economic and trade relations. Japan is one of our main trading partners and is the second largest source of imports at 12.4 percent or US$3.59 billion of the total import bill for the period January to April 2017. Japan also ranks first in terms of export with receipts valued at US$3.09 billion, for a total trade value of US$6.68 billion for the same period. Recently, several agreements to further enhance economic and security cooperation have been signed by our nations. Among the agreements reached were: the creation of business opportunities through Official Development Assistance (ODA) and private sector investments to spur infrastructure projects, including the promotion of agricultural businesses, as well as building capacity for maritime security. We can thus look forward to further strengthening of the bilateral relations between our countries, particularly in light of ongoing initiatives to pursue massive infrastructure projects. It is worth noting that under its Partnership for Quality Infrastructure program, the Japanese government announced in 2015 its plan to actively support the construction of modern infrastructure in the neighboring Asian nations. As a result of this plan, the Philippines and Japan committed to cooperate on the roadmap for better transport infrastructure in the Metropolitan Manila area by 2030, taking advantage of the Japanese technology and the ODA. As BSP Governor, I would like to take this opportunity to give information on the favourable prospects for growth and investments in the Philippines for Japanese investors and firms. Ladies and gentlemen, the Philippines' macroeconomic fundamentals remain solid and intact. They provide a stable anchor for sustained expansion, amid lingering volatilities and uncertainties coming mainly from the external environment. Recent economic data shows that in the first quarter of 2017, real GDP grew by 6.4 percent. Economic expansion remains broad-based with notable rebound in both the agriculture and exports sectors. The Philippines is still one of the best performing economies in the region. In fact, the overall confidence index of businesses for the second quarter of 2017 has improved, reflecting optimism in the economic prospects of the country. This is also evident in the sustained inflows of foreign direct investment which registered at USD 1.6 billion net inflows in the first quarter of 2017. I have said that I am blessed to continue building on the legacy of my predecessor, Governor Amando M. Tetango, Jr. as the sustained strength of the Philippine economy was underpinned by manageable inflation, adequate gross international reserves, and a steady stream of inflows from overseas Filipinos (OFs) remittances, revenue from the BPO sector and tourism income. These contribute to higher consumption spending. These are fundamentals that we will build on and continue during my term as BSP Governor. Under my term, the BSP will ensure that an enabling monetary and financial environment is maintained to achieve the country's growth objectives, while safeguarding price and financial stability. That is the macroeconomic picture. In the banking system, full liberalization of foreign banks' entry in the Philippines under Republic Act (R.A.) No. 10641, has allowed increasing presence of foreign banks in the country. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation was the first foreign bank branch to operate in the Philippines after the enactment of the law in July 2014. Meanwhile, Ogaki Kyoritsu Bank, Ltd. (OKB) was authorized by the Monetary Board, was also authorized to open a Representative Office in the Philippines in May 2017. Overall, there are 5 Japan-based banks in the Philippines (i.e., 3 foreign bank branches and 2 representative offices). The entrance of foreign banks facilitates the flow of investments, promoting trade, supporting business expansion, and encouraging technology transfers, leading to job creation and more productive output. This enhanced synergy between local and foreign banks will also create greater opportunities for service and product innovation in the banking system. Against this backdrop, Japanese investors in the country can look forward to expanded opportunities for growth and investments. There is this Japanese movie, a Kurosawa classic, The Seven Samurai. Are you familiar with it? In the movie there is insight on a Japanese decision-making process were information is gathered, deliberated on and analysed. The movie highlights the importance of discussion, and consensus-reaching. The process is time-consuming but recognizes that collaboration leads to the best decisions. I believe that too. Under my stewardship, the BSP will continue to do its part to strengthen strategic relations between our countries to foster stronger collaboration. For one, the BSP will continue to commit to our bilateral arrangements with the Bank of Japan in the interest of strengthening monetary and financial cooperation and integration. As a former Monbusho scholar and alumnus of GRIPS, I was privileged to receive excellent education and training in public sector policy formulation and management. This training aided me in my work as a policymaker and career official at the BSP. In my current capacity as Governor, I hope to pass on this legacy of kaizen, excellence and integrity to others as I serve my country with the new mandate given to me. I am grateful for your partnership in this regard. Thank you Philippines-Japan Society and the Philippines-Japan Economic Cooperation Committee for hosting this dinner and for the invitation to speak tonight. Arigatou gozaimasu. Maraming salamat. I wish everyone a pleasant evening.

Title: Information Security in Nation Building
Location: SMX Aura Convention Center, BGC, Taguig
Occasion: Annual Information Security Officers Group (ISOG) Summit 2017
Speaker: Nestor A. Espenilla, Jr.
Text: Co-workers in government - the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT), National Privacy Commission and BSP, information security professionals, ladies and gentlemen, good morning! Thank you for inviting the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to speak at your annual Information Security Officers Group (ISOG) Summit 2017. This Summit is very timely as we face growing threats from cyber-crime. I would like to begin by briefly recalling the growth story of the Philippine economy and the domestic banking system. A strong and resilient economy moves a nation forward. That is why through the years, our focus has been on ensuring sound macroeconomic fundamentals and developing the same as an organic source of resilience. Our economy has weathered two (2) major financial crises in the last two decades - the Asian financial crisis and the more recent global financial crisis. But the country also managed to register 73 consecutive quarters of GDP growth and earned investment grade status along the way. And the trend continues. GDP for the first quarter of 2017 continued to grow by 6.4 percent and GDP growth for 2017 is estimated to be among the highest in the world, making the Philippines one of "the fastest growing economy in the fastest-growing region in the world". The Philippine banking system has grown into a P13.8 trillion industry in terms of total assets as of the end-March 2017. Deposits of the banking industry have reached a record high of P10.6 trillion as of same date. Net bank lending was broad-based across industry sectors, posting a year-on-year growth of 17.8 percent to P7.7 trillion as of end-March 2017. Our strong fundamentals and sound banking system have contributed to the Philippines' standing as an attractive investment destination. In order to sustain growth of the whole economy and the banking system, secure, reliable and robust infrastructures and systems need to be in place to facilitate various economic activities. The financial sector, as a key component of the economy, should take the lead in this aspect. Nevertheless, the story of our economic growth would be more meaningful when positive effects and impact are felt by all in our society. Fortunately, advances in technology have enabled the development of solutions that enhance market reach and expand delivery channels. Through technology, people from all walks of life, including those in unbanked and underserved markets, can have access to formal financial services that can uplift their quality of life. Technology gives consumers access to their funds, potentially anytime, anywhere, at the touch of their fingertips. BSP-supervised financial institutions (BSFIs) embrace the digital age to streamline costs, maximize efficiency of their processes and manage risks across various facets of their operations. However, technological innovation is not without its downside. Cybercriminals exploit advances in technology to expand, conceal and carry out fraudulent activities, usually for gain, that can also undermine public trust and confidence in the financial system. It is in this area that information security can play a critical role in the grand objective of nation building. Increased economic activity from innovation can only be best assured if we have secure and reliable technologies that we can count on. The Information Security Officers Group (ISOG) has a crucial role to play in equipping information security officers with the technical expertise as well as raising the credibility of the discipline by encouraging professional qualifications. Your active role as specialist risk managers can go a long way in supporting the overall enterprise risk management efforts of your respective institutions. This will then pave the way for sound financial institutions that eventually form part of a strong and resilient national economy. Cybersecurity is high on the BSP's agenda because a single debilitating attack can permanently damage an institution's reputation and can also cause widespread economic loss, which may erode public's confidence in the financial system. While most of these risks are already being addressed by BSFIs as well as BSP's regulatory initiatives, malicious actors are continuously evolving, making their attack methods more complex, prevalent and sophisticated. Against this background, the BSP aims to provide an enabling environment that promotes innovation, while at the same time, ensuring a safe and secure digital banking environment. The BSP has implemented various regulatory reforms and strengthened its supervisory capacity to ensure that BSFIs adopt sound technological infrastructure. Regulations were put in place as early as year 2000 allowing banks to engage in electronic banking that is supplemented by appropriate risk management and consumer protection measures. The BSP is continuously working to ensure that financial industry participants are sensitive to and proactive in addressing emerging cyber threats. During the first half of 2017, we issued several regulations aimed at mitigating the effects of technology-related risks in BSFIs. These regulations address various facets of technology such as social media risk management, business continuity management and multi-factor authentication, among others. Recent issuances also include specific guidance on managing fraudulent e-mails and websites as well as combatting ransomware and other forms of malware attacks. To further heighten resilience against advanced forms of cyberthreats and risks, the enhanced guidelines on information security management are being finalized and will be released soon. The enhancements place a renewed focus on information security and clearly set the BSP's supervisory expectations as to cybersecurity controls and strategies and how these fit into the overall information security program of BSFIs. Beyond merely enforcing compliance, the BSP has forged partnerships and expanded collaborative arrangements with a wider stakeholder base. In addition to existing collaborative mechanisms with domestic financial industry associations, the BSP established strategic partnerships for purposes of strengthening financial surveillance, improving policy engagements and fostering dialogue. In closing, you can be assured that the BSP will remain steadfast in working to strengthen the banking system, improve risk management standards, and align our financial regulations with best practices and leading standards. I trust we can count on the industry's active participation and cooperation as we work towards securing our financial infrastructure. By keeping our information society secure and prudently harnessing digital innovation, we can realize our vision of delivering a high quality of life for all Filipinos. Thank you and have a productive summit in the next two days.

Title: Central Banking & Symphonies
Occasion: BSP's 24th Anniversary
Speaker: Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.
Text: Happy anniversary Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas! Ladies and gentlemen, we celebrate the 24th year of the BSP on a high note. Just last month, the Singapore-based publication The Asian Banker named the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas as the Best Macroeconomic Regulator in Asia-Pacific. The Asian Banker also presented the BSP Governor with a "Lifetime Leadership Achievement Award", citing the central bank's contributions to the Philippine financial system and the economy under his watch. Last May, a report published by the international credit rating agency S&P said our "central bank has a record of supporting sustainable economic growth and responding appropriately to changing economic circumstances." S&P added that our "ability to maintain macroeconomic and price stability through an economic cycle has been tested, including a period of exogenous shocks." And last February, the Hong Kong-based publication FinanceAsia named the BSP Governor "Outstanding Achievement Awardee" for excellent stewardship of the BSP, managing the difficult task of keeping inflation under control at the same time as giving the country room to grow and fulfill its potential. FinanceAsia cited our contributions to Philippine economic development and to the improvement of central banking standards in the region. Indeed fellow BSPers, our monetary and banking policies have continued to provide the stability needed by our economy to overcome the humps and bumps, and the twists and turns in the global landscape, including the Global Financial Crisis and its lingering effects on economies and central banks. Here in the Philippines, we did not only survive the GFC, we continue to thrive. Ladies and gentlemen of the BSP, we accomplished this together. BSPers, past and present, lahat may kontribusyon! As I keep saying, the BSP is not a one-man band. The individual and the institutional awards we receive belong to ALL BSPers across the country - mula Luzon, Visayas at Mindanao! Thank you and congratulations BSPers! The way I see it, the role of a central bank governor has a lot in common with that of a musical conductor, who leads people from different disciplines to create beautiful harmonies that add up to masterful symphonies. Of course, there were times we heard some discordant notes. But by and large, we played harmonious and beautiful music together, so to speak, that resulted in benefits for our people! Let me cite some highlights of our performance: We achieved low and stable inflation conducive to sustained economic growth by adopting data-driven and forward looking policies; We have a sound, stable and liquid banking system that is well-capitalized and supports the financing needs of our economy particularly the productive sectors; We operate a safe and reliable payments system that minimizes possible systemic risks and inspires confidence in our financial system; We have nurtured a strong external position that provides buffers to potential shocks to the economy and the financial system; and We are implementing a comprehensive agenda for financial inclusion to ensure inclusive growth that improves the quality of life of Filipinos. Given these positive outcomes, how do these play out and benefit our economy and our people? The first and most notable positive change is the transformation of the Philippine economy -- from being described as the sick man of Asia, we have moved up as a rising tiger economy whose growth is among the fastest in the region. In cooperation with other institutions, we have achieved the ideal convergence of low inflation amid high economic growth. Definitely, the size of the economy has been expanding -- from an average GDP growth of 4.9 percent from 2005 to 2010, growth went up to an average of 6.1 per cent in 2011 to 2016 and reached 6.4 percent in the first quarter of 2017. On the other hand, inflation averaged 5.2% in my first six years as Governor (from 2005 to 2010) and dropped to 3.0% in my second term (2011 to 2016). From January to May this year, inflation has remained stable and averaged 3.1%. The second positive outcome of our policies is the strengthening of our domestic banks, particularly in terms of size, capitalization and reach. The banking system has tripled in size over the past decade, with year-on-year growth of 12.6 percent. As of end-April 2017, the total resources of the banking system reached P14 trillion, the highest on record. Parallel to this, banks' overall capitalization is at levels above both the national requirement and the international BIS standard. As the main provider of domestic credit, the Philippine banking system is seen by international debt watchers as a source of sovereign strength. The third benefit is the continued increase in the volume and value of PhilPASS transactions -- from its modest start in 2002 with 5,685 transactions, first quarter 2017 transactions alone already hit 419,455 while value of transactions shot up from P2.4 trillion in 2002 to P78.7 trillion in the first quarter 2017. Indeed, confidence in the BSP's PhilPass supports the continued growth and development of our financial system. The fourth improvement is the sustained build-up of the country's foreign exchange reserves-- from a GIR level of $18.5 billion enough to cover about 4.6 months' worth of imports of goods and services in 2005, our import cover had moved up to about 9 months on a GIR of $82.2 billion as of end May 2017. At the same time, the country's debt management program saw external debt-to-GDP improve by more than half -- from 59.7 percent of GDP in 2005 to 24.0 percent as of end-March 2017. The fifth benefit is the country's elevation to investment grade beginning 2013. Major international credit rating agencies (i.e., Moody's, Fitch, and S&P) uniformly acknowledge the BSP as one of the institutional pillars that generates positive marks for the country. Ladies and gentlemen, the BSP has been able to accomplish all these because, as an institution, the BSP is ready. It is nimble enough to be able to adapt to the changes in its operating environment. We have built capacity among our people, streamlined processes, leveraged off technology as appropriate, and inculcated an overall sense of good governance and accountability in all that we do. In recent years, we have also institutionalized the new norm of financial stability in our organization as well as in policy coordination and cooperation with other financial regulators. This new mindset has allowed us to put on a more holistic lens in the conduct of surveillance and the crafting of policy. So far, so good. Looking ahead, I see the BSP successfully pursuing its mandate to help provide stability and promote sustained growth of our economy through monetary and banking policies. Ladies and gentlemen. We thank President Rodrigo Roa Duterte for having chosen the path of stability and continuity by appointing veteran central banker Nestor Espenilla, Jr. as our new BSP Governor. With Gov Nesting's deep knowledge of the BSP -- its history, mandate, organization, and corporate culture - he can certainly hit the ground running. I have worked closely with him and I can tell you that Gov Nesting is a top-notch central banker and a man of integrity, who has what it takes to excel as the BSP's new leader. Let us also welcome the three appointees of the President who will join the Monetary Board for a term of six-years each -- former trade secretary and veteran banker Peter Favila who returns to the MB; former economic planning secretary and eminent economist Dr. Phillip Medalla who was reinstated for another term at the Board; and veteran banker and corporate CEO Antonio Abacan. They complete the seven-man MB with Finance Secretary Sonny Dominguez; former general counsel and deputy governor of the BSP Juan de Zuniga, Jr.; veteran banker and former PDIC Head Val Araneta; and Monetary Board Chairman and BSP Governor Nestor Espenilla, Jr. I am very pleased to see therefore that we have with us distinguished guests who can provide crucial support and cooperation to move the BSP's agenda forward under Gov Nesting's watch. With us this morning are former Central Bank governors and colleagues, fellow workers in government, representatives from the banking sector, the business community, multilateral agencies, our friends from the media and the members of our families. Indeed, it is fitting that we have multi-sectoral representations today as BSP's policies ultimately affect all Filipinos, our economy and our country. I hope therefore that Gov Nesting and all the Members of the Monetary Board will receive all the support they need to craft, formulate, innovate and implement effective policies and programs to serve the best interest of our people, our economy and our country. Finally, I want to thank all of you for the unstinting support you have given me during my 43-years of service as a central banker, the last 12-years of which was as Chairman of the Monetary Board and Governor of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas. In particular, I am privileged and honored to have worked shoulder to shoulder with members of TEAM BSP--members of the Monetary Board, Management, officers and staff across the country. Your dedication to the pursuit of the BSP's mandate runs deep and strong, knowing that what is at stake could affect the quality of life of our people and our future as a nation. You are true public servants. Salamat sa inyo! On behalf of my family - my wife Elma, my daughters Eula and Mia, my son Patrick and his wife Miko together with my unica apo Zara, my brothers and sisters-- I thank you all. We are grateful that in sickness and in health, you were always there for me giving support, even singing and dancing to cheer us on. Maraming, maraming salamat sa inyo! Today, as I leave the BSP as citizen Say, I will not say goodbye. Instead, I will say... until we meet again. Mabuhay si Governor Nesting at ang Monetary Board! Mabuhay ang Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas! Mabuhay ang ating Inang Bayan! Mabuhay po tayong lahat!

Title: Continuing the Voyage of Excellence to a Bright Tomorrow
Location: BSP Assembly Hall, BSP Complex, Manila
Occasion: 24th Anniversary Program of the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP)
Speaker: Nestor A. Espenilla, Jr.
Text: Outgoing Governor Amando M. Tetangco, Jr.; distinguished members of the Monetary Board - Finance Secretary and MBM Carlos Dominguez III, MBM Felipe Medalla, MBM Juan De Zuñiga, Jr., MBM Valentin Araneta, MBM Antonio Abacan, and MBM Peter Favila; outgoing MBM members Alfredo Antonio and Armando Suratos; esteemed former Central Bank Governors Jaime Laya, and Jose Cuisia, Jr.; former MB Members - Raul Boncan, Ignacio Bunye, Melito Salazar, and Vicente Valdepeñas; distinguished guests from the banking community, the business sector, and the academe; my co-workers in the BSP in Manila, Quezon City, the regions, and the branches; family and friends, including my wife Tess and my children Jackie, Nikko and Nesty; ladies and gentlemen, good morning! First of all, I wish us all a happy 24th anniversary! Celebrating BSP's Brand of Excellence Our chosen theme for this anniversary is "excellence", highlighting one of the BSP's core values. Together with patriotism, dynamism, integrity, and solidarity, excellence is the defining imprint in every BSPer's DNA. These values should describe who we are and what we always aspire to be in our everyday life in BSP.
